stories.headline: Nvidia unveils DSX POD, containerized Vera Rubin AI factories that deploy in 14 days

key_facts.fact: At GTC Berlin on October 21, 2026, Nvidia introduced DSX POD, a reference design for complete Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers and validated before delivery.
key_facts.excerpt: GTC Berlin—NVIDIA today introduced DSX POD, a reference design for complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories built by partners inside modular containers, integrated and validated before delivery.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia says factory-built units cut deployment time at a prepared site from six months to as little as 14 days, with deliveries worldwide starting in early 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Factory-built units reduce deployment time at a prepared site from six months to as little as 14 days... to deliver modular AI factories worldwide in early 2027.

key_facts.fact: Each DSX Pod packs seven Vera Rubin racks into a shipping-container-sized unit weighing about 28,000 kg that can travel by truck on normal roads; Nvidia gave no price, but analysts estimate a single Vera Rubin rack costs more than $7 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia's new DSX Pod AI Factory packages seven Vera Rubin AI racks in a shipping container designed to be transported by truck... weighs about 28,000 kilograms... analysts estimate a single Vera Rubin rack can cost more than $7 million.

key_facts.fact: Partners building DSX PODs include Anduril, Bull, Crusoe, DayOne, Dell, Foxconn (Ingrasys), Gigabyte, HPE, Lenovo, Pegatron, Quanta, Schneider Electric, Vertiv and Wistron.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA is working with Anduril, Armada, Bull, Crusoe, DayOne, Dell Technologies, Delta, Eaton, Foxconn (Ingrasys), GIGABYTE, HPE, Lenovo, Pegatron, Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT), Schneider Electric, Vertiv and Wistron

key_facts.fact: Nvidia claims its DSX designs, using closed-loop liquid cooling and dry coolers, can cut facility cooling water use to near zero, saving 54 million liters a day at 2-gigawatt scale, and that DSX MaxLPS software produces the same tokens with up to 30% less power.
key_facts.excerpt: potential savings of 54 million liters a day for a 2-gigawatt deployment... NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS software helps operators use up to 30% less power to generate the same number of tokens

key_facts.fact: Huang said on stage that DSX POD is 'a complete transformation of the world supply chain' that will change how data centers are installed and built.
key_facts.excerpt: "This is a complete transformation of the world supply chain," Huang said. "This will change the way that people install and build data centers, and hopefully, as a result, velocity goes up."

key_facts.fact: Huang has said Nvidia's content per gigawatt of data-center capacity rose from about $18 billion to $40-plus billion.
key_facts.excerpt: "What we offer into one gigawatt went from about $18 billion or so per gigawatt, to $20-something billion per gigawatt, to now $40-plus billion per gigawatt," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said recently on a podcast.

stories.headline: Agile Robots and Nvidia launch research humanoid, plan up to 2,000 units in 2027

key_facts.fact: At GTC Berlin on October 21, Munich-based Agile Robots announced Agile ONE SN, a full-stack reference humanoid preconfigured with Nvidia's Isaac GR00T model and powered by Nvidia's Jetson Thor computer.
key_facts.excerpt: Agile Robots announced Agile ONE SN, a full-stack reference humanoid preconfigured with NVIDIA Isaac GR00T and powered by the NVIDIA Jetson Thor edge AI platform.

key_facts.fact: The robot stands 1.40 meters, weighs 40 kg, has 31 degrees of freedom, carries 3 kg per arm and has two five-finger hands with 20 degrees of freedom each and tactile sensing; it is scheduled for early 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: standing 1.40 meters (4.59 feet tall) and weighing 40 kilograms (88 pounds), with 31 degrees of freedom and a 3-kilogram payload per arm... Dual WUJI Hand 2 five-finger hands, each offering 20 degrees of freedom... Scheduled to be available in early 2027

key_facts.fact: Agile Robots CEO Zhaopeng Chen told Reuters the company plans to produce 1,000 to 2,000 of its compact humanoids next year, with production of the ONE S and ONE SN models starting by the end of 2026, aimed at universities and corporate labs; Stanford and ETH Zurich are among potential customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Germany's Agile Robots plans to produce up to 2,000 petite humanoid robots next year under a partnership with Nvidia announced on Wednesday targeting universities and corporate research labs... Production of Agile ONE S and ONE SN models will begin by the end of this year

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang said 'the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching' as Nvidia expanded its Isaac platform with an Isaac OS runtime and Isaac Lab 3.0.
key_facts.excerpt: "General-purpose robotics is advancing at extraordinary speed — the ChatGPT moment for robotics is fast approaching," said Jensen Huang... NVIDIA Isaac platform adds new Isaac OS runtime, Isaac Lab 3.0 for robot learning

key_facts.fact: Agile Robots, a 2018 spin-off of the German Aerospace Center (DLR) backed by SoftBank and Xiaomi, is targeting about €640 million in revenue in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Agile Robots was founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center, known as DLR... Its investor list includes SoftBank and Xiaomi. Agile Robots is aiming for revenue of approximately €640 million in 2026.

key_facts.fact: Agile Robots currently produces about ten robots per day at its new Fürstenfeldbruck factory, which is running at 20% utilization.
key_facts.excerpt: Etwa zehn Roboter pro Tag produziert Agile Robots laut Sexton aktuell in Fürstenfeldbruck... Aktuell sei die Fabrik zu 20 % ausgelastet.

stories.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix upgrade China fabs to 200+ layer NAND to fend off YMTC

key_facts.fact: Samsung and SK Hynix are upgrading their China factories to make NAND flash chips with more than 200 layers, on par with their South Korean output, four people told Reuters; both companies confirmed upgrades were underway in close consultation with Washington.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung and SK Hynix confirmed in statements to Reuters that upgrades were underway and were being done in close consultation with Washington... the two companies are working to manufacture flash NAND memory chips with more than 200 layers at their Chinese plants

key_facts.fact: Under an internal project called 'Monami', Samsung is converting its Xian plant, about 40% of its global NAND output, to 286-layer V9 NAND, targeting 5,000 wafers a month in December 2026 and 40,000 by December 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: As part of a project known internally as "Monami"... Samsung is converting the facility to make 286-layer V9 NAND chips, aiming for monthly output of 5,000 wafers in December 2026 and then a jump to 40,000 wafers by December 2027

key_facts.fact: Samsung said the upgrade complies with US export rules and that it is not expanding production capacity or building new facilities.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said the upgrade complied with U.S. export regulations... It added that it was not expanding production capacity or building new facilities.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix wants to move its Dalian plant, the sole fab of its Solidigm unit, from 192-layer to 240-plus-layer NAND, and may seek US permission for R&D on 300-plus-layer chips there.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix is looking to switch to producing NAND products with 240 layers or more at its Dalian facilities... It currently makes products with 192 layers there... may seek permission from Washington to conduct research and development on 300-plus-layer chips

key_facts.fact: Since 2025, BIS has said it does not intend to grant licenses to upgrade technology or expand capacity at foreign chipmakers' China fabs, and Reuters could not determine whether licenses for the needed equipment have been granted.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security also said in 2025 it did not intend to grant licences to upgrade technology and expand capacity... Reuters could not, however, determine to what extent US authorities have granted export licences

key_facts.fact: China's YMTC held 38.5% of China's NAND market in Q2 2026, up from 28% in 2025 and overtaking Samsung, whose share fell to 33.5% from 36%; SK Hynix's fell to 17% from 20%, per Omdia.
key_facts.excerpt: YMTC's market share in China's NAND market reached 38.5% in the second quarter of this year, rising from 28% annually last year and overtaking Samsung Electronics. During the same period, Samsung Electronics' share fell from 36% to 33.5%, and SK hynix's share dropped from 20% to 17%.

stories.headline: NextDC shares plunge ~42% as Melbourne power delay forces a one-third guidance cut

key_facts.fact: On October 21, Australian data-center operator NextDC cut its FY2027 net revenue guidance to A$475M-A$500M from A$615M-A$640M and underlying EBITDA to A$245M-A$265M from A$385M-A$410M.
key_facts.excerpt: The data center operator expects underlying EBITDA of A$245 million to A$265 million for the year ending June 30, 2027, down from A$385 million to A$410 million. Net revenue guidance fell to A$475 million to A$500 million from A$615 million to A$640 million.

key_facts.fact: The cut stems from power distributor Jemena suspending grid upgrade works for NextDC's M3 data center in West Footscray, Melbourne, amid resident opposition; the next grid supply increase is now expected in fiscal 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: NextDC attributed the revised estimates to delays to electricity network upgrades by energy supplier Jemena, required to increase power supply to its M3 data centre in West Footscray.

key_facts.fact: NextDC shares closed down 41.72% at A$5.35 on the ASX, their worst drop since listing in 2010, wiping about A$2 billion off its market value.
key_facts.excerpt: the shares traded 41.72 percent lower on the Australian Securities Exchange, closing Wednesday's trading at A$5.35.

key_facts.fact: NextDC put all new development projects and land acquisitions on hold and lowered FY2027 capex guidance to A$4.5B-A$5B from A$5.25B-A$5.75B.
key_facts.excerpt: NextDC lowered its fiscal 2027 capital expenditure guidance to A$4.5 billion to A$5 billion from A$5.25 billion to A$5.75 billion... The company put all new development projects and land acquisitions on hold

key_facts.fact: CEO Craig Scroggie said NextDC has no plans to raise equity and could sell some data-center developments, a move the WSJ said dealt another blow to AI-trade sentiment ahead of Anthropic's IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: Australia's NextDC said it could sell some data center developments amid a darkened earnings outlook, triggering a 42% share-price fall and dealing another blow to sentiment on the artificial intelligence trade ahead of Anthropic's blockbuster IPO.

key_facts.fact: The affected M3 contracts accounted for about A$140 million each of net revenue and EBITDA in August guidance and include service-level credits and, in some cases, customer termination rights.
key_facts.excerpt: The revised figures exclude the affected M3 customer contracts, which made up about A$140 million each of net revenue and underlying EBITDA in the company's August guidance... In some circumstances they give the customer rights to terminate.

stories.headline: Nvidia in talks to invest hundreds of millions in Firmus after its IPO flop

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is in discussions to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in Australian AI cloud company Firmus Grid after it abandoned its IPO, The Information reported on October 20.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) is in discussions to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in Firmus Grid Ltd. after the Australian AI cloud company abandoned an initial public offering, the Information reported.

key_facts.fact: The move signals Nvidia will keep supporting neoclouds, debt-laden AI cloud providers; Nvidia is already an investor in Firmus, owning around 7%.
key_facts.excerpt: The US tech company, the world's most valuable, owns around 7pc of Firmus.

key_facts.fact: Firmus had been expected to list at a valuation of up to A$44 billion before cancelling, blaming market volatility.
key_facts.excerpt: Firmus had been expected to go public at a valuation of up to A$44bn (£23bn) before cancelling plans. It blamed "recent market volatility and prevailing market conditions".

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is also preparing to invest $1 billion in Nscale next month, as equity if Nscale has listed by then or as convertible debt if not, according to the Telegraph report.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is preparing to invest $1bn in Nscale next month, either as an equity investment if the company has gone public by then, or as convertible debt if the IPO does not happen.

key_facts.fact: CoreWeave shares have fallen more than a quarter in the past month while yields on its debt have soared.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares in CoreWeave, one of the biggest neoclouds, have fallen by more than a quarter in the last month, while yields on its debt have soared.

stories.headline: AI data-center IPOs wobble: Nscale touts $100B+ backlog, DayOne weighs cutting its listing

key_facts.fact: Nscale CEO Josh Payne told staff in a memo that the UK AI data-center operator has more than $100 billion in contracted revenue and 'insatiable' demand, and still plans a New York IPO by end-2026 at a $30-35 billion valuation, the FT reported on October 21.
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale CEO Josh Payne told staff by memo the company has more than $100bn in contracted revenue and still plans a year-end 2026 New York IPO at $30bn-$35bn.

key_facts.fact: Of Nscale's roughly $103 billion total contracted value as of August 31, only $2.6 billion is active; Microsoft and Anthropic together account for about 85%.
key_facts.excerpt: Only $2.6bn of the $103bn backlog Nscale disclosed as of 31 August is active, with Microsoft and Anthropic together holding roughly 85% of the total.

key_facts.fact: Nscale posted a $1 billion net loss on $141 million revenue in H1 2026; some IPO investors have reportedly pushed for a $16-19 billion valuation, and Microsoft pulled out of a planned Nscale site in Essex.
key_facts.excerpt: Investors were said to believe the company... should be valued at between $16 billion and $19 billion... The company reported a net loss of $1 billion on revenue of $141 million during the first half of 2026.

key_facts.fact: Singapore-based DayOne Data Centers is weighing a delay of its US IPO or a smaller listing raising $2.5-3 billion, about half the up-to-$5 billion it originally sought at a roughly $20 billion valuation, Bloomberg reported on October 21.
key_facts.excerpt: The Singapore-based firm may cut fundraising to US$2.5 billion-US$3 billion, down from an earlier target of up to US$5 billion and a US$20 billion valuation.

key_facts.fact: DayOne, backed by Coatue and Hillhouse, filed for a US IPO earlier in October with Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citigroup leading; no final decision has been made.
key_facts.excerpt: DayOne filed for a US IPO earlier in October. The offering is being led by Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America and Citigroup... Deliberations are ongoing and DayOne has not made any final decisions

key_facts.fact: DayOne is a spinoff of China's GDS Holdings and filed to list American depositary shares on Nasdaq under the ticker DODC.
key_facts.excerpt: The GDS-spinoff had filed for a Nasdaq debut under ticker DODC aiming at a potential $20 billion valuation.

stories.headline: Micron signs labor deal with Taichung union; Taoyuan strike threat remains

key_facts.fact: On October 21, Micron Memory Taiwan and the union representing its Taichung workers signed a labor-management agreement covering several issues and withdrew from mediation scheduled for October 22; terms were not disclosed.
key_facts.excerpt: In a joint statement, Micron and the Taichung union said they had signed an agreement covering several issues after constructive negotiations and had canceled a mediation session scheduled for Thursday. Details of the agreement have not been disclosed.

key_facts.fact: Micron employs about 12,300 workers in Taichung and 3,000 in Taoyuan, of whom about 11,000 and 2,400 respectively belong to the local unions.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron employs about 3,000 workers in Taoyuan and 12,300 in Taichung, of whom about 2,400 and 11,000, respectively, belong to the local unions.

key_facts.fact: The unions have demanded a long-term mechanism distributing 15% of Micron's operating profits to employees.
key_facts.excerpt: The unions have demanded a long-term mechanism under which 15 percent of Micron's operating profits would be distributed to employees

key_facts.fact: The deal came a day before the Taoyuan union's planned one-day strike; the Taoyuan dispute remains unresolved and its union urged Micron to present a profit-sharing proposal.
key_facts.excerpt: The agreement came a day before the Taoyuan union's planned one-day strike, which was timed to coincide with the Thursday mediation session. The Taoyuan union said it remains open to talks and urged the company to present a reasonable plan.

key_facts.fact: Taoyuan union members had authorized a strike on October 7, with 1,994 of 2,012 votes cast in favor.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron's Taoyuan union said on Oct. 7 that it had secured authorization to strike after six days of voting, with 1,994 of the 2,012 members who cast ballots supporting the action.
